purpose: A bounded operating method for the regulated foundation of a Medicare-focused insurance practice: mapping the layered rule sources that govern each act and the precedence between them; establishing and maintaining the authority stack as requirement classes (state producer licensing, upline and carrier contracting and appointment, the annual industry certification, per-carrier product certification and ready-to-sell status) in a register that answers 'may I speak to this person about this plan today' with evidence; reading regulated compensation as a mechanism to be verified rather than a number to chase, and sizing the carrier shelf so that need rather than pay can decide every comparison; classifying every material and act as marketing or communication and routing it through the required review; running permission-to-contact, scope-of-appointment, prohibited-practice, third-party-marketing, call-recording, event and community-presence rules as daily habits rather than remembered facts; protecting a predominantly older and frequently vulnerable clientele through disclosure-first, unpressured, comprehension-checked contact; and keeping a contemporaneous, retained file per interaction that survives a carrier audit, a secret shop or a complaint, all gated behind a pre-season readiness check that must be green before the first beneficiary hears one word about a plan.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is an individual licensed agent or a very small independent agency enrolling beneficiaries in Medicare-related and health plans, not a carrier employee, a call-center floor manager, or a field marketing organization running a recruiting downline

federal marketing and communication requirements for Medicare Advantage and prescription-drug plans, state producer-licensing and unfair-trade-practice rules, telemarketing and do-not-call regimes, privacy obligations, and carrier-specific policies all differ by jurisdiction, by carrier and by contract year, so every requirement here is named as an obligation class whose current specifics must be verified with the applicable regulator, carrier and counsel before acting

compensation, recoupment on rapid disenrollment, fair-market-value limits and administrative payments are treated as regulated mechanisms whose current published values must be read from the current-year schedule for the specific product and state; no amount, percentage or income figure is asserted anywhere in this knowledge base

the people served are predominantly older adults and people with disabilities, a protected and frequently vulnerable population, so disclosure-first contact, pacing, comprehension checks and stop rules are treated as operating requirements rather than courtesies

the durable asset of this practice is a clean compliance record plus a served book, and carrier access can be closed by a single sustained violation pattern, so growth is always planned inside the rule set rather than against it
exclusions: the enrollment-period system as the demand calendar (initial, annual and special enrollment classes), need-driven comparison across coverage types, drug-coverage and provider-network fit, and the compliant enrollment conversation with its required artifacts - that is the enrollment periods, plan comparison and needs fit knowledge base this one hands off to

renewal-compensation mechanics over the life of an enrolled account, the year-round service model for plan changes, provider issues and drug-cost events, annual-review practice, retention through service quality, and compliant book growth through referrals - that is the renewal compensation, service and compliant retention knowledge base

personalized plan, medical, financial, tax or legal advice to any beneficiary or caregiver; this knowledge base is operator education about how the practice is licensed, certified, contracted and permitted to communicate, and the enrollment decision always belongs to the beneficiary

specific commission amounts, fair-market-value caps, renewal or administrative payment figures, override amounts, lead prices, event budgets or income figures; compensation appears only as a mechanism to be read from the current-year schedule and verified per case

jurisdiction-specific and year-specific particulars such as pre-licensing hours, examination content, continuing-education credit counts, appointment timing windows, scope-of-appointment lead times and retention durations, call-recording retention periods, event reporting deadlines and nominal-value thresholds, all of which appear only as obligation classes to be verified against current rules in the relevant jurisdiction

any solicitation, marketing, comparison or enrollment activity attempted before the producer license, carrier appointment, annual certification and per-carrier ready-to-sell status are all in force and evidenced
plan-specific benefit claims, star-rating claims, superiority claims or any statement implying government endorsement or that the practice speaks for the Medicare program
recruiting other agents, building a downline agency, and the economics of overrides earned on other producers' production
clinical guidance about drugs, conditions, providers or treatment choices, and any referral arrangement structured as an inducement to enroll rather than as a permitted, disclosed relationship

competency_questions.question: What exactly must be in force before I may say one word to a beneficiary about a Medicare plan, and how do I prove on any given day that it still is?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRACTICE_SCOPE_CHARTER states what the practice does and refuses, PRODUCER_LICENSE_FOOTPRINT gives the state licensing requirement classes and the artifact each produces, and SELLING_AUTHORITY_LEDGER supplies the per-carrier per-state per-plan-year register that returns a dated go/no-go answer with evidence

competency_questions.question: Which rulebooks govern a given act, and which one wins when the program rules, my state, and the carrier's own policy disagree?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_AUTHORITY_MAP names the layers that apply per act and the strictest-applicable precedence rule, and MARKETING_VS_COMMUNICATIONS_TEST shows how the classification of the act selects which layer's obligations attach

competency_questions.question: What does the annual certification season actually require of me, in what order, and by when must each piece be finished so I can sell on day one of the marketing window?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANNUAL_CERTIFICATION_CYCLE describes the annual industry certification and compliance modules as a calendar with attempt limits, CARRIER_PRODUCT_CERTIFICATION describes the per-carrier product training that follows it, and ANNUAL_READINESS_GATE states the pre-season composition that must be green before contact

competency_questions.question: How do contracted, appointed, certified and ready-to-sell differ, and which one actually authorizes me to present a specific plan to a specific person in a specific state?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARRIER_CONTRACTING_AND_APPOINTMENT separates the carrier paperwork from the state appointment filing, CARRIER_PRODUCT_CERTIFICATION names ready-to-sell as the only status that authorizes presenting and enrolling, and SELLING_AUTHORITY_LEDGER shows where each status is verified before an appointment is booked

competency_questions.question: How do I choose the upline or field marketing organization I write under, and what does that choice cost me if I want to move a carrier relationship later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HIERARCHY_AND_RELEASE_TERMS names the commission-assignment and release-policy clauses to read before signing and the dormancy consequence of a wrong assignment, and PORTFOLIO_BREADTH_AND_STEERING_GUARD shows how a blocked carrier relationship distorts the shelf the practice can honestly offer

competency_questions.question: How does the money in this business actually come to exist, and how do I keep it out of the recommendation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPENSATION_MECHANISM_LITERACY describes initial and renewal categories, fair-market-value limits and rapid-disenrollment recoupment as regulated mechanisms read from the current-year schedule rather than memorized figures, and PORTFOLIO_BREADTH_AND_STEERING_GUARD states the written rule that compensation is never a comparison factor or a tiebreak

competency_questions.question: Is this flyer, post, script or phone call marketing or communication, and what review must it pass before it reaches a beneficiary?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKETING_VS_COMMUNICATIONS_TEST gives the intent-and-content test and the routing rule to the carrier or program review path, and DIGITAL_PRESENCE_AND_MATERIAL_REVIEW applies it to every beneficiary-facing surface with version, approval identifier and plan-year stamp

competency_questions.question: When am I permitted to contact this person at all, what does their permission actually cover, and when has it gone stale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERMISSION_TO_CONTACT_DISCIPLINE defines consent as a dated artifact bounded by topic, channel and duration that never transfers to a relative, and TPMO_RULES_AND_LEAD_VENDOR_VETTING states how a purchased lead's consent trail is verified before any outreach

competency_questions.question: What must be agreed and recorded before a personal appointment, and what do I do when the beneficiary raises a product class we never agreed to discuss?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_OF_APPOINTMENT_PRACTICE gives the pre-appointment agreement class, its product-type naming and the documented-expansion move for mid-meeting drift, and DOCUMENTATION_AND_RETENTION_SYSTEM states where the signed artifact lives and how long it is kept

competency_questions.question: What conduct is flatly prohibited, and where does the line sit in the ordinary situations I face - a pharmacy aisle, a clinic waiting room, a neighbor's kitchen, a health fair booth?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROHIBITED_PRACTICES_INVENTORY enumerates the prohibited conduct classes with the plain sentence to say when a beneficiary asks for one of them, and COMMUNITY_PRESENCE_AND_REFERRALS distinguishes permitted common-area presence from prohibited activity where care is delivered

competency_questions.question: How do I run events and a community presence that actually produce business without turning an educational session into a prohibited sales event?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EDUCATIONAL_VS_SALES_EVENTS states the class declaration, the materials and collection limits of each class and the drift hazard, and COMMUNITY_PRESENCE_AND_REFERRALS gives the partner relationships that are permitted and the inducement line they must not cross

competency_questions.question: How do I buy or generate leads without inheriting somebody else's consent problem and answering for their advertising?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TPMO_RULES_AND_LEAD_VENDOR_VETTING gives the disclaimer obligation class, the consent-trail evidence to demand from a vendor and the shared-lead hazard, and DIGITAL_PRESENCE_AND_MATERIAL_REVIEW gives the lead-form language and claims discipline for leads the practice generates itself

competency_questions.question: What file must exist for each interaction so that a carrier audit, a secret shop or a complaint ends with the record speaking for me, and how long is each piece kept?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOCUMENTATION_AND_RETENTION_SYSTEM lists the per-interaction artifacts, the custody rules for identity and health data and the contemporaneity principle, CALL_RECORDING_AND_RETENTION covers the recording obligation and retrieval deadline, and OVERSIGHT_AUDIT_AND_COMPLAINT_RESPONSE shows how the file is used when an allegation arrives

competency_questions.question: How do I protect a beneficiary who may be vulnerable, and at what point do I stop selling and refer instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_BENEFICIARY_SAFEGUARDS states the disclosure-first, unpressured, comprehension-checked practice and the stop rule that routes to a second conversation, a documented authorized representative or the neutral state assistance program, and PRACTICE_SCOPE_CHARTER supplies the refusal sentence that keeps the decision with the beneficiary

glossary.definition: The state-issued authority to transact insurance in named lines, held as a resident license in the agent's home state and as nonresident licenses elsewhere; it authorizes the person rather than any particular product, carries an expiration date and a continuing-education obligation, and must be current in the state where the beneficiary is met.

A carrier's filing with a state that authorizes a specific licensed producer to solicit that carrier's business in that state; it is per carrier and per state, some states require it before the first application while others allow a just-in-time filing, and a license alone never authorizes selling a particular carrier's plan.

The plan-year training and scored assessment covering Medicare basics, marketing rules, and fraud, waste and abuse that carriers require before an agent may sell Medicare Advantage or prescription-drug products, commonly satisfied by an industry course of the AHIP class; it expires every plan year and has attempt limits set by the course and the carriers.

The carrier-portal state confirming that a specific agent has cleared contracting, appointment, annual certification and that carrier's own product training for a named product, plan year and state; it is the only status that authorizes presenting or enrolling, and it can be revoked mid-year by a compliance finding or a missed recertification.

A documented, affirmative request from a beneficiary to be contacted, bounded by the topic, product class and channel it names and by a staleness period after which it must be refreshed; it is what makes outreach lawful, it never transfers from one person to a spouse, child or neighbor, and it sits underneath separate telemarketing and do-not-call duties.

The documented agreement, obtained before a personal marketing appointment by a defined lead time, in which the beneficiary states which product types may be discussed; it bounds the meeting, must be expanded on the record before another product class is discussed, and is retained for a required period.

The rule class covering entities and agents that generate, sell or use leads and market plans on behalf of or alongside carriers; obligations include a prescribed disclaimer stating that the agent does not offer every plan available in the area, disclosure of how many carriers are represented, and responsibility for how the leads being used were generated.

Content whose intent is to draw attention to a plan or influence an enrollment decision, or that mentions benefits, premiums, cost sharing, comparisons or ratings; it carries the stricter obligation set including required disclaimers, prohibited claims and a review or submission path, and it is distinguished from the broader communications class by intent and content rather than by format.

An event advertised and run as instruction about how the program and coverage classes work, at which plan-specific promotion, scope agreements and enrollment applications are not permitted; it is the counterpart of a marketing or sales event, which may discuss plan-specific content and lead to enrollment but carries reporting and advertising obligations.

The formal record created when a beneficiary complaint about an agent or an enrollment reaches the plan and the program; it triggers a carrier response deadline, is answered from the interaction file and recording rather than from memory, and clusters of them against one agent or one lead source drive audits, corrective action and contract termination.

nodes.definition: Write down, before any beneficiary hears one word about a plan, what this practice does, what it refuses to do, and the exact sentence used when a request crosses that line. A Medicare-focused practice educates beneficiaries about how the coverage classes work, presents the plans it is licensed, appointed and certified to present, discloses that it does not offer every plan available in the area, and helps the beneficiary act on the beneficiary's own decision. It does not make medical, tax or legal judgments, does not tell a person which physician or drug to choose, does not promise that a plan will cover a particular claim, and does not present a plan it is not ready to sell. The charter names the product classes offered, the neutral destinations an out-of-scope question is referred to (the plan's own member services, the state health insurance assistance program class, the federal Medicare help line, the beneficiary's clinician or attorney), and the standing sentence that the enrollment decision belongs to the beneficiary. It exists because scope collapses in the exact moment a trusting seventy-eight-year-old asks what the agent would do, when the honest answer is a structured comparison plus a referral rather than an opinion.

included: the product classes the practice offers and the categories it declines
the referral destinations for medical, legal, tax and program-eligibility questions
the standing disclosure and decision-ownership language every conversation carries
excluded: the plan comparison itself and how needs are matched to coverage types, which belongs to the enrollment periods and plan fit knowledge base
in-force service promises and annual-review commitments, which belong to the renewal and retention knowledge base

pros.claim: A written refusal list turns the hardest live moments into a rehearsed sentence instead of an improvisation under social pressure
pros.example: a beneficiary asking whether she should stop a prescribed medication to lower her drug costs gets the referral sentence to her prescriber rather than an opinion the agent is not licensed to give

pros.claim: Naming the neutral destinations up front makes the practice look more trustworthy, not less capable, to exactly the population that has been cold-called for months
pros.example: handing a caller the state assistance program's number when they need help with a program-eligibility question they cannot afford to get wrong

cons.claim: A charter drawn too tightly makes the agent decline work a properly licensed and certified agent could legitimately do, which sends people back into the cold-call market for no protective benefit
cons.example: refusing to explain how the drug-coverage class generally works because the charter confused general education with personalized medical advice

cons.claim: A charter that lives only as a document changes nothing unless the scripts, website copy and event language actually match it
cons.example: a homepage headline promising to find the best plan while the charter says the agent presents only the plans it carries

failure_modes: scope that lives only in the agent's head and quietly moves whenever a large or emotional case pushes on it
marketing copy that implies the practice speaks for the Medicare program or offers every plan in the area
answering a medical, tax or eligibility question conversationally because saying it is outside my scope feels unhelpful in the moment
acceptance_tests: the charter names the offered product classes, at least three refusal categories each with the destination it is referred to, and the decision-ownership sentence, and every script, page and event handout uses that same language
a randomly chosen public asset can be read side by side with the charter with no claim in the asset exceeding it
revisit_triggers: a product class, carrier or state is added to or removed from the practice
a regulator, carrier or errors-and-omissions carrier restates what an agent may say or claim
a complaint or audit finding alleges the practice stepped outside its stated scope

base.update_signal: the practice adds a product class, carrier or state, or a compliance source restates what an agent may claim or must disclose

nodes.definition: Build a one-page map of who actually governs each act in this business and which rule wins when two of them disagree. Four layers apply at once. Federal program rules for Medicare Advantage and prescription-drug plan marketing and communications are published for each contract year and reissued with changes. State insurance-department rules license the person and police unfair trade practices, advertising, replacement conduct and senior-designation use. Federal and state telemarketing, do-not-call, texting and privacy regimes govern the channel rather than the content. Each carrier's own policies, frequently stricter than the floor, are enforceable through the contract and the ready-to-sell switch. The map records, for each ordinary act - an outbound call, a mailer, a social post, a kitchen-table meeting, a booth at a health fair - which layers apply, what evidence proves compliance, and where the current authoritative text is published, because none of it is memorizable: it changes by contract year and by state. The operating rule the map encodes is that the strictest applicable requirement governs, that silence in one layer is not permission in another, and that an upline saying it is fine is never an authority.

included: the four rule layers and which apply per ordinary act
the strictest-applicable precedence rule and where each layer's current text is published
the refresh ritual at each contract-year turn
excluded: legal interpretation or opinions on specific rule text, which belongs to qualified counsel and the regulator itself
enrollment-period mechanics and plan rules, which belong to the enrollment knowledge base

pros.claim: Mapping layers per act converts an unmemorizable body of rules into a lookup an agent can actually run before doing something
pros.example: checking before sending a birthday postcard whether it lands in the marketing class, needs a disclaimer, and touches the do-not-mail rules the state adds

pros.claim: Writing down where the authoritative text lives makes annual re-verification cheap instead of a rumor-driven scramble
pros.example: reopening the same three published sources each contract year instead of relying on last season's slide deck from an upline meeting

cons.claim: A map is a snapshot and quietly goes stale, which is more dangerous than having no map because it feels authoritative
cons.example: an agent applying last year's mapping of a texting rule that changed at the contract-year turn

cons.claim: Layer mapping cannot resolve genuine ambiguity, and treating the map as a legal opinion invites confident errors
cons.example: reading silence about a novel social-media format as permission rather than as a question for the carrier's compliance desk

failure_modes: treating the carrier's guidance as the whole rule set and missing state advertising or telemarketing duties
assuming that what is common practice among local agents reflects what is permitted
carrying a prior contract year's mapping into a new plan year without re-reading the current text
acceptance_tests: for each of at least six ordinary acts the map names the applicable layers, the evidence of compliance, and the published source consulted, with the date it was checked
the precedence rule is written as an operating sentence and can be applied to a case where the carrier policy is stricter than the program floor
revisit_triggers: a new contract year's marketing and communications requirements are published
a state adopts or amends advertising, senior-designation, texting or do-not-call requirements
a carrier issues a policy bulletin that tightens a practice the map currently permits

base.update_signal: a new contract year's rules are published, a state amends its advertising or telemarketing requirements, or a carrier bulletin tightens an act the map currently treats as permitted

nodes.definition: Establish and keep in force the state authority to transact the health lines this practice sells, in every state where a beneficiary will be met, and treat it as a maintained asset rather than a one-time examination. The requirement classes are a resident producer license in the appropriate line of authority for health and, where the shelf includes them, the life or accident-and-health lines used with senior clients; a nonresident license for each additional state, which most states issue on the strength of the resident license; a continuing-education obligation with its own credit composition and a renewal cycle with hard deadlines; and a duty to report name, address and administrative-action changes inside a stated window. Each class has an issuing authority, a renewal date, and an artifact that proves current status on demand. The practice keeps one row per state with those dates plus a reminder set well ahead of each deadline, because a lapse does not merely pause selling: business written while unlicensed can be voided, compensation reversed, and the lapse reported to other states and carriers. Fees, credit counts, examination content and reinstatement windows differ by state and change, so verify current requirements with each state insurance department.

included: resident and nonresident license classes for the lines the practice sells
continuing-education and renewal obligation classes with their proving artifacts
the change-reporting duty and the per-state date register
excluded: state-specific hours, fees, credit counts and examination content, which are verified with each department rather than asserted here
carrier appointment, which is a separate authority handled in the contracting node

pros.claim: A dated per-state register makes lapse a scheduling problem rather than a discovery made during an audit
pros.example: a nonresident renewal reminder firing sixty days out for the neighboring state where the agent meets a handful of clients each year

pros.claim: Knowing the line of authority precisely prevents the quiet error of discussing a product class the license does not cover
pros.example: an agent licensed only in the health line recognizing that a life-based final-expense conversation requires a line the license does not carry

cons.claim: Maintaining a wide multi-state footprint costs continuing-education time and renewal fees whether or not the states produce business
cons.example: keeping three nonresident licenses current for a handful of snowbird clients who may not renew with the practice

cons.claim: License status alone creates a false sense of readiness because it authorizes nothing carrier-specific
cons.example: an agent with a perfect license record who is still prohibited from taking an application because the carrier appointment was never filed

failure_modes: letting a nonresident license lapse in a state that still holds two or three active clients
missing the continuing-education composition requirement and completing credits that do not satisfy the renewal
failing to report an address or administrative-action change inside the required window and discovering it at renewal
acceptance_tests: every state where a beneficiary may be met has a row showing license number, line of authority, effective and expiry dates, continuing-education status and the date the status was last verified with the department
a reminder exists for each renewal and continuing-education deadline with lead time long enough to complete the requirement
revisit_triggers: a client relocates or a marketing plan extends into a new state
a state changes its renewal cycle, continuing-education composition or reporting duties
an administrative action, name change or address change occurs that must be reported

base.update_signal: a state amends licensing, continuing-education or reporting requirements, or the practice adds a state or a line of authority

nodes.definition: Complete the annual, program-level training and testing that carriers require before they will allow an agent to sell Medicare Advantage or prescription-drug products for the coming plan year, and complete it early enough that everything downstream still fits in the calendar. The requirement class is an annual industry certification covering Medicare basics and the marketing rules, commonly satisfied by a course of the AHIP class with a scored assessment and a limited number of attempts, plus fraud-waste-and-abuse and general compliance modules, all refreshed every plan year. Carriers publish which courses they accept, how results are transmitted, and the date after which an uncertified agent cannot be ready to sell for that year. The work is fundamentally calendar work: certification opens on a schedule, per-carrier product training cannot start until it is complete, ready-to-sell status cannot be granted until product training is complete, and the marketing window opens on a fixed date whether or not the agent is finished. Attempts are finite and the assessment is long, so the disciplined agent books the sitting deliberately rather than squeezing it between appointments. Verify each year's accepted courses, attempt limits and deadlines with each carrier, since they differ and they move.

included: the annual industry certification and compliance module classes and their attempt structure
the sequencing constraint that gates product certification and ready-to-sell status
the per-carrier acceptance and transmission question
excluded: the content of Medicare coverage rules themselves, which belongs to the enrollment and plan-fit knowledge base
per-carrier product training, which is its own node

pros.claim: Finishing certification early converts the whole pre-season into slack instead of a queue where one failed attempt cascades
pros.example: clearing the assessment in the first days it opens so that four carriers' product modules can run in parallel afterwards

pros.claim: The annual refresh is the one forced moment each year when the marketing rules are actually re-read rather than remembered
pros.example: an agent discovering during the annual module that a contact practice used all last year was tightened for the new plan year

cons.claim: The certification consumes a large block of pre-season time in the same weeks contracting, material review and event planning compete for attention
cons.example: an assessment sitting colliding with the deadline to submit event advertising for carrier review

cons.claim: Passing an annual test creates a feeling of currency that does not extend to state or carrier-specific rules the course never covers
cons.example: an agent who passed the annual course confidently texting a prospect in a state with its own messaging restrictions

failure_modes: starting certification in the last window before the deadline and exhausting the attempt limit
completing a course a particular carrier does not accept and discovering it when ready-to-sell is withheld
treating the certificate as proof of authority to sell rather than as one prerequisite among four
acceptance_tests: the annual certification and compliance modules are complete, with completion evidence stored and the transmission to each carrier confirmed in that carrier's portal before the pre-season deadline
the certification date sits far enough ahead of the marketing window that every downstream product certification could still be completed if one attempt failed
revisit_triggers: a carrier changes which certification it accepts or moves its deadline
a new plan year opens the certification cycle
a carrier is added to the shelf after the season has started

base.update_signal: a carrier changes accepted courses, attempt limits or deadlines, or the plan-year certification cycle opens with revised content

nodes.definition: Decide, before the first carrier contract is submitted, which upline or field marketing organization the practice writes under and on what terms, because that assignment is sticky and expensive to undo. What is actually being chosen is who supplies training, lead programs, quoting and enrollment tools, back-office support and access to errors-and-omissions coverage; how compensation is assigned and paid, whether directly from the carrier or assigned through the hierarchy; what the release policy is when the agent later wants to move a carrier relationship, since carriers commonly impose a dormancy period without a signed release before an agent may re-contract elsewhere; and whether lead-repayment obligations, production requirements, book-servicing rights or non-solicitation terms attach. The discipline is to read the release clause and the compensation-assignment clause first and the recruiting pitch last, and to keep a signed copy of what was actually agreed rather than the brochure. The cost of a careless assignment is concrete: it can lock the practice out of the one carrier the local hospital system contracts with for a full waiting period, which quietly distorts every comparison the agent can honestly present during that time.

included: the clauses that decide portability: release policy, dormancy, compensation assignment, non-solicitation
the support and tooling actually provided versus promised
the pre-contract decision ritual and the signed-copy requirement
excluded: recruiting other agents and building a downline, which is outside this practice model entirely
specific override or compensation figures, which are read from current schedules rather than asserted

pros.claim: Reading release terms before signing preserves the ability to reshape the shelf later, which is the only defense against being locked into a narrow set of carriers
pros.example: declining an attractive support package whose contract required assignment of compensation and a long dormancy on release

pros.claim: A well-matched organization supplies the operational scaffolding a solo agent cannot build alone, especially quoting tools, compliance review and errors-and-omissions access
pros.example: using the organization's material-review desk to get an event flyer approved with lead time instead of guessing

cons.claim: The decision is made with the least information, at the start, and its consequences arrive years later
cons.example: discovering only when a local plan changes networks that re-contracting with the needed carrier requires a release the current upline will not sign

cons.claim: Support and lead programs create obligations that can pull the practice toward the organization's preferred carriers rather than the beneficiary's needs
cons.example: a lead-credit program that effectively subsidizes production with one carrier while the local need points elsewhere

failure_modes: signing the first contract handed over at a recruiting meeting without reading the release and assignment clauses
keeping no signed copy and relying on a verbal promise about release when the relationship sours
choosing an organization for its lead offer while ignoring which carriers it can actually contract
acceptance_tests: the signed agreement is on file and its release, dormancy, compensation-assignment, production and non-solicitation clauses are summarized in the practice's own words with the page references
the decision memo names at least one alternative that was compared and the specific reason this organization was chosen
revisit_triggers: the practice needs a carrier the current hierarchy cannot contract
the organization changes its release policy, lead program or support model
a local network or plan change makes an uncarried carrier necessary to serve the area honestly

base.update_signal: the organization restates its release, assignment or production terms, or the practice needs a carrier the hierarchy cannot reach

nodes.definition: Size the carrier shelf so that the honest answer to a beneficiary's need is normally available on it, and install the written guard that keeps compensation out of the comparison. The judgment has two failure directions. Too narrow, and the practice systematically pushes people toward the carriers it happens to hold, which is the mechanism by which well-meaning agents end up steering without ever intending to; the tell is a service area where the dominant hospital system or the most-used pharmacy chain sits with a carrier the agent does not carry. Too broad, and the annual certification, product-training and portal burden explodes, leaving the agent shallowly acquainted with everything and genuinely expert in nothing, which is its own harm to beneficiaries who need someone who knows how a specific plan behaves in practice. The method is to inventory what the local population actually needs - the plan classes present in the county, the major provider systems, the common drug situations, the languages spoken - contract for coverage of those needs, and write down the referral rule for the case the shelf cannot serve. The guard is a standing rule that compensation differences are never a comparison factor and never a tiebreak; the shelf exists so that rule can be kept without costing the beneficiary.

included: how many and which carriers to contract, sized against local provider systems and population needs
the written no-steering guard and the referral rule for needs the shelf cannot serve
the disclosure that the practice does not offer every plan in the area
excluded: the per-client comparison of specific plans and their benefits, which belongs to the enrollment periods and plan fit knowledge base
clinical judgments about providers or drugs, which belong to the beneficiary's clinicians

pros.claim: A shelf built from local need removes the structural pressure that turns a good agent into a steering agent
pros.example: carrying the carrier contracted with the county's dominant hospital system so a beneficiary loyal to that system never has to be talked out of it

pros.claim: A written referral rule gives the agent a dignified exit when the shelf genuinely cannot serve someone
pros.example: referring a beneficiary whose specialist sits only in an uncarried plan to the neutral state assistance program rather than steering them to a second-best fit

cons.claim: Every added carrier adds an annual certification, a portal, a product update cycle and a set of forms, and the burden compounds each plan year
cons.example: an agent carrying so many carriers that the pre-season certification load spills past the date the marketing window opens

cons.claim: Breadth alone does not prevent steering if the practice never writes the guard down and never audits its own recommendation mix
cons.example: a shelf of six carriers where nearly every enrollment lands with one, and nobody has asked why

failure_modes: building the shelf from what the upline can contract rather than from what the service area needs
adding carriers for compensation reasons and discovering the certification burden in the pre-season crunch
never reviewing the distribution of enrollments across the shelf, which is the only early signal of unintended steering
acceptance_tests: the shelf is justified in writing against a named inventory of local provider systems, plan classes and common beneficiary situations, with the gaps and the referral rule stated
the no-steering guard is written as a standing rule and the practice can produce a periodic review of how enrollments distribute across the shelf with an explanation for any concentration
revisit_triggers: a major local provider system changes which carriers it contracts with
a plan exits the service area or a new plan class enters it
the practice's own enrollment mix concentrates on one carrier without a need-based explanation

base.update_signal: local provider contracting changes, a plan enters or exits the service area, or the practice's own enrollment mix concentrates without a need-based explanation

nodes.definition: Get formally contracted and appointed with each carrier whose plans the shelf needs, and keep straight what each step authorizes. Contracting is the carrier's own paperwork: an application with license evidence, background and eligibility screening including the federal exclusion and debarment list classes, banking and tax details, an errors-and-omissions coverage requirement in most cases, and the compensation agreement itself. Appointment is the carrier's filing with a state that authorizes this producer to solicit that carrier's business there; it is per carrier and per state, some states require it before the first application while others permit a just-in-time filing tied to the first piece of business, and a license alone never authorizes selling a particular carrier's plan. The visible outputs are a writing number per carrier and an appointment status the agent can evidence on demand. Because the contracting queue lengthens as the season approaches and background screening has its own latency, this work is scheduled months ahead of the marketing window rather than in the week before it. Confirm each state's appointment timing rule and each carrier's current requirements directly rather than assuming they match the last carrier's.

included: carrier contracting paperwork and eligibility screening classes
state appointment filing per carrier and per state and its timing classes
writing numbers, errors-and-omissions requirements and the evidence of status
excluded: per-carrier product training and ready-to-sell status, which is the next node
hierarchy and release terms, which are decided before contracting begins

pros.claim: Separating contracted from appointed prevents the most common authority error in the business
pros.example: an agent with a signed carrier contract pausing before a meeting because the appointment in the beneficiary's state has not been filed

pros.claim: Scheduling contracting months early absorbs the latency of background screening and carrier queues without touching the selling season
pros.example: submitting contracting paperwork in the spring so a screening question can be resolved long before certification opens

cons.claim: Contracting broadly creates ongoing obligations and production expectations with carriers the practice may barely use
cons.example: an unused carrier contract that still demands annual certification and product training to stay active

cons.claim: Carrier requirements and state timing rules differ enough that a process learned at one carrier misleads at the next
cons.example: assuming just-in-time appointment applies in a state that requires the appointment filed before any solicitation

failure_modes: starting contracting inside the certification season and losing the first weeks of the marketing window
assuming an appointment covers every state where the carrier operates rather than only those filed
letting errors-and-omissions coverage lapse and having contracts suspended without noticing
acceptance_tests: for every carrier on the shelf there is a signed contract, a writing number, evidence of appointment in each state where business will be written, and current errors-and-omissions coverage with dates
each state's appointment timing rule is recorded next to the carrier row and matches what the carrier and the state department currently state
revisit_triggers: a state or carrier changes its appointment timing or screening requirements
the practice adds a state, a carrier or a product line
an errors-and-omissions policy or a carrier contract approaches renewal or is suspended

base.update_signal: a carrier or state changes contracting, screening or appointment timing requirements, or the practice adds a carrier, state or product line

nodes.definition: Complete each carrier's own product training and assessment for the plan year and product family, then confirm the resulting ready-to-sell status, which is the only status that actually authorizes presenting and enrolling. The pattern is consistent even though the details are not: the carrier accepts the annual industry certification, then requires its own modules covering its plans, its enrollment systems and its compliance policies, with an assessment and attempt limits; when the last requirement clears, the carrier's agent portal flips the agent to ready-to-sell for named products, plan year and states. The distinction that matters operationally is that contracted is not appointed, appointed is not certified, and certified is not ready-to-sell: an agent can hold three of the four and still be prohibited from accepting an application. Status is also revocable mid-year by a missed recertification, a compliance finding, an expired license or a contract action, and carriers do not uniformly warn before flipping it. The habit is to verify status per carrier, per state and per product before any appointment is booked, and again after any carrier notice, treating the portal as the authoritative record rather than an email from a colleague.

included: per-carrier product training and assessment classes and their attempt limits
ready-to-sell confirmation per product, plan year and state and how it is verified
mid-year revocation causes and the re-verification habit
excluded: the annual industry certification itself, which is its own upstream node
the substance of plan benefits and comparison, which belongs to the enrollment and plan fit knowledge base

pros.claim: Treating ready-to-sell as the only real authorization removes an entire class of unauthorized-sale exposure
pros.example: declining to take an application at the kitchen table because the portal shows certification complete but ready-to-sell still pending for that state

pros.claim: Carrier product training is where the operational details that actually help beneficiaries are learned, not just a compliance hurdle
pros.example: learning a carrier's enrollment platform quirks before season rather than while a beneficiary waits at the table

cons.claim: The per-carrier modules multiply with shelf breadth and cluster into the same pre-season weeks
cons.example: four carriers releasing product modules within the same two weeks, each with its own portal and assessment

cons.claim: Ready-to-sell status is a carrier-controlled switch that can flip without warning, so a stale check is worse than none
cons.example: a status verified in September that was revoked in October after a license renewal posted late

failure_modes: assuming ready-to-sell carries across states or product families when it is granted per product and state
checking status once before the season and never again
letting an assessment attempt limit expire mid-season and losing the ability to write that carrier for the plan year
acceptance_tests: for every carrier and product the practice intends to present, the portal shows ready-to-sell for the current plan year and the relevant state, with the verification date recorded
a re-verification runs before each booked appointment and after every carrier notice, and its result is written into the authority register
revisit_triggers: a carrier issues a recertification requirement or a compliance notice mid-year
a license or appointment lapses or is renewed late
a new product family or state is added to the plan-year shelf

base.update_signal: a carrier changes its product-training requirements or flips ready-to-sell status, or a new product family or state enters the plan-year shelf

nodes.definition: Learn how the money in this business actually comes to exist, as a regulated mechanism to be read and verified rather than a number to chase. The structure an agent must be able to explain: compensation for Medicare Advantage and prescription-drug enrollments is constrained by a fair-market-value framework set for each contract year, with a distinct initial-year amount and a lower renewal amount, and with rules deciding which enrollment situations pay at the initial rate and which pay at the renewal rate; carriers may separately pay administrative amounts under their own published rules; supplement products sit under different schedules set by carrier and state; and rapid disenrollment triggers recoupment classes that reverse compensation when a beneficiary leaves within a defined window. The operating skills are reading the current-year schedule for each carrier and product, classifying a given case correctly before it is written, reconciling what was actually paid against what the schedule says, and explaining the mechanism plainly and without discomfort when a beneficiary asks how the agent is paid. Published amounts change every year and vary by state and product, so nothing is memorized here: it is read from the current schedule and verified per case. Compensation is a fact about the practice, never an input to a recommendation.

included: initial versus renewal categories, fair-market-value limits and recoupment as mechanisms
reading and reconciling the current-year schedule per carrier, product and state
the plain-language answer when a beneficiary asks how the agent is paid
excluded: any specific amount, percentage, cap or income figure, which must be read from the current published schedule
renewal-compensation administration over the life of the book, which belongs to the renewal and retention knowledge base

pros.claim: Understanding the mechanism lets the agent answer the compensation question honestly on the spot, which defuses the suspicion most beneficiaries arrive with
pros.example: explaining that the carrier pays a regulated amount set for the year and that it does not vary in a way that would favor one plan in the comparison

pros.claim: Reading the schedule before writing prevents surprise reversals and lets the practice plan cash timing around known recoupment windows
pros.example: recognizing before submission that a particular enrollment situation falls in the renewal category rather than the initial one

cons.claim: Studying compensation closely creates the very salience the no-steering rule must suppress, and awareness alone does not neutralize it
cons.example: an agent who has just reconciled a statement finding one carrier's plans coming to mind first in the next comparison

cons.claim: Schedules are year-specific, product-specific and state-specific, so any remembered figure is wrong soon and confidently wrong
cons.example: quoting last plan year's structure to a colleague after the current year's schedule has already changed

failure_modes: treating a headline number from an upline recruiting deck as the schedule
never reconciling statements, so an underpayment or an unnoticed recoupment persists for months
allowing compensation knowledge to leak into the order in which plans are presented
acceptance_tests: the current-year compensation schedule for each carrier and product on the shelf is on file with the date it was retrieved, and the practice can classify a sample case into its correct category with the schedule in hand
a written answer exists for the question of how the agent is paid, using mechanism language and no invented figures, and it matches what the schedules say
revisit_triggers: a new contract-year compensation schedule is published or a carrier restates its administrative payment rules
a statement reconciliation shows an unexplained difference or an unexpected recoupment
the practice adds a product class with a different compensation structure

base.update_signal: a new contract-year schedule is published, a carrier restates administrative payments, or reconciliation surfaces an unexplained difference

nodes.definition: Maintain one register that answers, in seconds and with evidence, the question of whether the agent may speak to this person about this plan today. It holds one row per carrier per state per plan year carrying license status and expiry, appointment status and its filing date, annual certification completion, per-carrier product certification completion, ready-to-sell confirmation with the date it was verified, the writing number, and errors-and-omissions coverage dates. It is refreshed at defined moments rather than continuously: at every carrier notice, at each license or coverage renewal, when the certification season opens, and immediately before any appointment with a beneficiary is booked. The register exists because the four authority layers expire on four different calendars maintained by four different parties, none of whom reliably warns the agent first; it collapses a scattered set of portal states into a single go or no-go signal that survives time pressure. Its second job is evidentiary: when a carrier audit or a state inquiry asks what authority existed on a particular date, the register plus the underlying artifacts answer immediately instead of being reconstructed months later from memory and screenshots.

included: the row structure covering license, appointment, certification, ready-to-sell, writing number and coverage dates
the refresh moments and the pre-appointment go or no-go check
the evidentiary use of the register in an audit or inquiry
excluded: the underlying qualification work itself, which lives in the licensing, contracting and certification nodes
beneficiary-level records of what was discussed, which live in the documentation system

pros.claim: One register turns four expiring authorities into a single check an agent can actually perform before every appointment
pros.example: catching that ready-to-sell for one carrier lapsed in a second state before a beneficiary meeting there is confirmed

pros.claim: Dated verification entries make the practice's authority provable retrospectively, which is exactly what an inquiry asks for
pros.example: answering a state question about a March meeting with the ledger row and the portal screenshot captured that week

cons.claim: A register is only as good as its refresh discipline, and a stale row is actively misleading because it looks authoritative
cons.example: a row still showing ready-to-sell after a carrier suspended the agent pending a complaint review

cons.claim: Maintaining rows per carrier, state and product is real recurring administrative work that competes with selling in the busiest weeks
cons.example: re-verifying dozens of rows during the same days appointments are being booked at their densest

failure_modes: copying last plan year's rows forward and changing only the year
recording status without the date it was verified, which destroys its evidentiary value
keeping the register somewhere the agent cannot open from a beneficiary's kitchen table
acceptance_tests: every carrier, state and product the practice intends to present has a row with all authority fields populated and a verification date inside the current refresh window
picking any past appointment at random, the register plus its artifacts show what authority was in force on that date without reconstruction
revisit_triggers: any carrier notice, suspension, contract action or product change
a license, appointment or errors-and-omissions renewal
the opening of a new plan-year certification season

base.update_signal: a carrier notice, suspension or renewal changes an authority field, or a new plan year resets the certification and ready-to-sell rows

nodes.definition: Apply, before anything is produced or said, the classification test that decides which rule set governs it. Program rules distinguish a broad class of beneficiary communications from the narrower class of marketing, using intent and content rather than format: material whose intent is to draw attention to a plan or influence an enrollment decision, or that mentions plan benefits, premiums, cost sharing, comparisons or ratings, generally falls in the marketing class and carries the stricter obligations - required disclaimers, prohibited claims, and a carrier or program review and submission path before use. General education that names no plans and steers toward none, and routine servicing communications with existing clients, sit outside it. The test is applied per artifact and per act, because the same sentence can land on opposite sides depending on what surrounds it: a benefit description inside a neutral explainer and the same description inside a mailer with a call to action are not the same thing. The practical output is a routing rule - classify first, route marketing-class items to the review path with real lead time, keep the approved version together with its approval identifier and plan-year stamp, and never publish the draft that was written while waiting.

included: the intent-and-content classification test and its per-act application
the routing rule to carrier or program review and the approval-identifier discipline
the boundary between general education, servicing communication and marketing
excluded: the specific review submission mechanics of any one carrier, which are read from that carrier's current instructions
the enrollment conversation itself, which belongs to the enrollment knowledge base

pros.claim: Classifying before producing prevents the expensive sequence of writing, printing, publishing and then recalling
pros.example: catching that a postcard mentioning a premium amount is marketing-class before five thousand of them are printed

pros.claim: A per-act test extends the same discipline to spoken acts and social posts that people rarely think of as material
pros.example: recognizing that a short video answering a plan-benefit question is marketing-class content even though it was recorded on a phone in the car

cons.claim: The boundary genuinely blurs at the edges, and reasonable agents classify the same borderline piece differently
cons.example: a neutral explainer that mentions one carrier by name only in a caption, which one reviewer calls education and another calls marketing

cons.claim: Routing everything conservatively into review creates lead-time drag that tempts the practice to publish first and review later
cons.example: a timely community announcement missing its moment because it sat in a review queue behind seasonal pieces

failure_modes: classifying by format rather than by intent and content, so a social post is treated as informal and skips review
reusing an approved piece after editing it, which voids the approval it still carries
treating silence about a new channel as permission to use it unreviewed
acceptance_tests: every beneficiary-facing item in the current inventory carries a classification, and each marketing-class item carries an approval identifier and a plan-year stamp
a borderline item can be walked through the intent-and-content test on paper, with the reasoning recorded and the conservative route taken when it stays ambiguous
revisit_triggers: the contract year's definitions of marketing and communications are restated
a carrier changes its review or submission path or its disclaimer requirements
the practice adopts a new channel or format not covered by the current classification

base.update_signal: the contract year restates the marketing and communications definitions, or a carrier changes its review path, disclaimer text or submission requirements

nodes.definition: Treat permission to contact as an artifact with a scope and a shelf life rather than a vague social license. The rule class prohibits unsolicited contact of beneficiaries: no unrequested visits to a home, no unsolicited calls, texts or emails to people who did not ask, no approaching people in common areas without an invitation, and no treating a referral as consent from the person referred. What creates permission is an affirmative, documented request from the beneficiary - a reply card or web form whose language plainly states what the person is asking for, a returned call to a number they left, an in-person request at a booth or event, or an inbound call. Permission is bounded by what it says: the topic and product class named, the channel agreed, and a staleness period after which it must be refreshed rather than assumed. It never transfers to a spouse, an adult child or a neighbor who was in the room. Layered on top are the telemarketing and do-not-call regimes with their own consent, scrubbing and identification duties per channel. The operating habit is simple and absolute: attach the consent artifact to the record before the first outreach, and if it cannot be produced, the outreach does not happen.

included: what does and does not create permission, and the artifact that evidences it
the topic, channel and staleness bounds and the non-transfer rule
the telemarketing and do-not-call overlay as a separate channel-level duty
excluded: the content of the conversation once contact is lawful, which belongs to the enrollment knowledge base
jurisdiction-specific staleness periods and scrubbing intervals, which must be verified currently

pros.claim: A consent artifact attached before outreach converts the most common complaint allegation into a document that answers it
pros.example: producing the dated web-form record with its exact request language when a beneficiary reports an unrequested call

pros.claim: Bounding permission by topic and channel keeps the practice from stretching one inquiry into a campaign the person never agreed to
pros.example: a person who asked about drug-coverage basics by email not being added to a call list for plan promotions

cons.claim: Strict consent discipline shrinks the reachable universe and makes the practice look slower than competitors who ignore the rules
cons.example: discarding a batch of purchased records whose consent language cannot be produced while a competitor calls them all

cons.claim: Consent language written by someone else may be technically present but too vague to survive a challenge
cons.example: a lead form whose fine print bundles insurance contact with unrelated offers so broadly that no specific request is evidenced

failure_modes: treating an event sign-in sheet as blanket permission for later calls
letting a stale permission from a prior plan year justify fresh outreach
calling a relative or neighbor mentioned during a conversation as if they had consented
acceptance_tests: every outbound contact record links to a dated consent artifact whose language names the topic and channel, and the record shows the check ran before the first attempt
a sample of contact records can be tested against the applicable do-not-call and channel duties without any record failing to produce its artifact
revisit_triggers: telemarketing, texting or do-not-call rules change in any state where the practice contacts people
a complaint alleges unrequested contact
a lead source changes its form language or its consent capture mechanism

base.update_signal: telemarketing, texting or do-not-call requirements change, a complaint alleges unrequested contact, or a lead source alters its consent language

nodes.definition: Run the scope-of-appointment ritual properly: before a personal marketing appointment, the beneficiary agrees in a documented form to which product types will be discussed, and the meeting then stays inside that scope. The requirement class includes an agreement obtained ahead of the meeting by a defined lead time, with narrow exceptions for walk-ins and unscheduled situations; a form naming the product types at issue, such as a Medicare Advantage and prescription-drug discussion as distinct from a supplement discussion; a record of who agreed, by what method and on what date; and a retention period for the artifact. Two moments decide whether it is done well. The first is framing: the agreement is explained as a consumer protection that keeps the meeting to what the beneficiary asked about, not as paperwork to be waved past on the way to the real conversation. The second is drift: when a beneficiary raises a product class outside the signed scope, the disciplined move is to document a new or expanded agreement on the record before discussing it, rather than sliding into it because the person seemed interested. Lead times, permitted formats, exceptions and retention durations are set by current rules and carrier policy, so verify them for the plan year.

included: the pre-appointment agreement class, its timing and format classes, and product-type naming
the framing script and the documented-expansion move for mid-meeting drift
who signs, how it is recorded and where it is retained
excluded: the plan comparison and enrollment application that happen inside the agreed scope, which belong to the enrollment knowledge base
specific lead-time and retention durations, which are verified against current rules

pros.claim: A properly framed scope agreement visibly narrows the meeting, which reassures a beneficiary who expected to be sold everything at once
pros.example: telling a couple that because they asked about drug coverage, that is all today's meeting will cover, and watching the room relax

pros.claim: A dated artifact makes the meeting's boundaries provable when an allegation says the agent pushed an unrelated product
pros.example: producing the agreement showing only the supplement discussion was agreed when a complaint claims an advantage-class plan was pushed

cons.claim: The lead-time requirement collides with how real appointments get made, especially with people who want help immediately
cons.example: a beneficiary calling on Friday for a Saturday meeting when the agreement window has not elapsed

cons.claim: Handled as bureaucracy, the ritual reads as confusing paperwork to an eighty-year-old and damages the trust it exists to protect
cons.example: a form pushed across a table with sign here and no explanation of what it does

failure_modes: collecting the agreement at the table because the meeting was booked in a hurry
discussing a second product class without expanding the scope on the record
keeping the artifact only in a phone photo that never reaches the beneficiary file
acceptance_tests: every personal marketing appointment has an agreement dated ahead of the meeting by the required lead time, or an explicitly documented exception, naming the product types discussed
any meeting whose topic expanded shows a documented expansion timestamped before the new product class was discussed
revisit_triggers: the rules change the lead time, permitted formats, exceptions or retention duration
a carrier requires its own form or a different signature method
a complaint or audit finding involves a discussion outside the agreed scope

base.update_signal: lead time, format, exception or retention requirements change, or a complaint involves a discussion outside an agreed scope

nodes.definition: Keep a written, current inventory of conduct that is flatly prohibited, each item paired with the ordinary situation in which it actually shows up and the plain sentence to say when someone asks for it. The classes include unsolicited direct contact of any kind - door-to-door, unrequested calls, texts and emails, and approaching people in common areas uninvited; marketing where care is delivered, such as exam rooms, hospital patient rooms, dialysis areas and the pharmacy counter, as distinct from common areas where permitted activity may occur with the provider's agreement; offering meals, gifts or prizes beyond the nominal-value class, or conditioning anything of value on enrollment; absolute superlatives, misleading statements, and any implication of government endorsement or that the agent is calling from Medicare; misuse of program names and logos; cross-selling non-health products during a Medicare marketing appointment; accepting enrollment applications at an event advertised as educational; and asking for referrals in a way that turns a private conversation into unsolicited contact of a third party. Each entry gets a plain-language refusal line the agent can say without embarrassment. The inventory is rebuilt each contract year from the current rule text rather than from memory, from a colleague's habits or from what the practice did last season.

included: the enumerated prohibited-conduct classes and the ordinary situations that trigger each
the plain refusal line for each item
the annual rebuild of the inventory from current rule text
excluded: state-specific nominal-value thresholds and setting-specific carve-outs, which must be verified currently
the enrollment conversation and application handling, which belong to the enrollment knowledge base

pros.claim: A pre-written refusal line makes the right answer available in the moment when the pressure is social rather than legal
pros.example: a beneficiary offering to introduce the agent to everyone at her bridge club, met with the line about how those neighbors have to ask first

pros.claim: Situating each prohibition in a concrete setting stops the list from being abstract knowledge that fails on contact with a real pharmacy aisle
pros.example: knowing before arriving that the table may sit in the store's common area but not at the pharmacy counter

cons.claim: Some boundaries are genuinely gray in real settings and an inventory can create false confidence at exactly those edges
cons.example: a clinic that calls its waiting area a common area while the rule turns on where care is actually delivered

cons.claim: A long list is only useful if it is rehearsed, and unrehearsed knowledge fails under the improvisation pressure of a live conversation
cons.example: an agent who knows the cross-sell rule but drifts into a life-product discussion when a client raises it warmly

failure_modes: learning the rules from what other local agents visibly do
carrying a prior-year inventory forward without checking the current text
treating a beneficiary's explicit request for a prohibited act as authorization for it
acceptance_tests: the inventory lists each prohibited-conduct class with its ordinary trigger situation and a refusal line, and cites where the current rule text was read and on what date
the practice can demonstrate rehearsal, for example a periodic run-through of the highest-pressure refusal lines before the season
revisit_triggers: a contract-year rule change adds, removes or narrows a prohibition
an enforcement action or carrier bulletin highlights a practice the inventory currently treats as acceptable
the practice enters a new setting such as a retail location, clinic partnership or health fair

base.update_signal: a contract-year change or enforcement action alters a prohibition, or the practice enters a setting the inventory has not addressed

nodes.definition: Understand what obligations attach when the practice markets as, or buys from, a third-party marketing organization, and vet every lead source as if the agent will personally answer for how the consent was obtained, because in practice the agent does. The obligation classes include a required disclaimer whose content is prescribed - stating in substance that the agent does not offer every plan available in the area and directing the beneficiary to the official program sources for the full set of options - together with disclosure, when asked, of how many carriers and plans the practice represents, and rules governing how leads may be generated, recorded, shared and used. Vetting a vendor means seeing the actual consent language the consumer saw, the timestamp and the originating page or call record, whether the lead was sold exclusively or shared among several agents, whether the advertising that produced it made prohibited claims, with fear-based hooks about losing benefits being the recurring offender, and what the contract says about indemnity, audit rights and the vendor's own compliance program. The economics are counterintuitive: a cheap lead with an unverifiable consent trail is not cheap, it is an unsolicited-contact complaint with a delay fuse, and the complaint attaches to the agent's record rather than the vendor's.

included: the disclaimer and representation-disclosure obligation classes
vendor vetting evidence: consent language, timestamp, origin, exclusivity, advertising claims, contract terms
the rule that responsibility for the contact travels to the agent who uses the lead
excluded: lead prices, cost per acquisition and marketing budget figures, which are the practice's own measured numbers rather than asserted values
the conversation that follows a lawful contact, which belongs to the enrollment knowledge base

pros.claim: Demanding the consent trail before purchase filters out the vendors whose entire model depends on the agent not asking
pros.example: asking for the originating page and timestamp for five sample records and receiving nothing verifiable, which ends the evaluation

pros.claim: Knowing the disclaimer obligation cold makes every first contact start honestly, which is also the best opening a suspicious beneficiary can hear
pros.example: opening a call by stating plainly that the practice does not offer every plan in the area and naming where the full set can be found

cons.claim: Verified-consent lead sources are scarcer and slower, and the practice competes against agents who accept unverifiable volume
cons.example: a season where the disciplined pipeline is thinner while competitors work a shared list of the same names

cons.claim: Even a well-vetted vendor can change its advertising mid-flight, so vetting is a recurring duty rather than a one-time approval
cons.example: a vendor quietly adding a scare-based headline to its landing page after the contract was signed

failure_modes: buying shared leads and calling people who have already told three agents to stop
accepting a vendor's assurance of compliance without seeing a single consumer-facing artifact
omitting the required disclaimer on first contact because the script was written before the obligation was checked
acceptance_tests: for every active lead source the practice holds the consumer-facing consent language, sample records with timestamps and origin, the exclusivity terms, and the contract's indemnity and audit clauses
the required disclaimer appears in every first-contact script and marketing-class asset, in the current prescribed substance, with the date the wording was last verified
revisit_triggers: the disclaimer or third-party marketing obligations are restated for a new contract year
complaints or opt-out requests cluster around one lead source
a vendor changes its advertising, its consent flow or its sharing model

base.update_signal: disclaimer or third-party marketing obligations are restated, complaints cluster on a lead source, or a vendor changes its consent flow or advertising

nodes.definition: Stand up the recording and retention machinery before the first sales call of the season, treating it as evidence infrastructure rather than a formality. The obligation class requires calls in the marketing, sales and enrollment chain to be recorded in their entirety and retained for a defined period, with carriers layering their own retention and production requirements on top, and with state two-party-consent laws adding a separate duty to announce recording in some jurisdictions. The operational work is unglamorous and decisive: a system that records reliably on every channel actually used including mobile, an announcement built into the opening script, file naming that ties each recording to a beneficiary record and a date, storage that is secure and access-controlled because the audio contains health and identity information, retention that runs the full required period without an automatic purge cutting it short, and retrieval fast enough to meet a carrier's response deadline. The failure that hurts is rarely a bad call; it is a missing one. When an allegation arrives and no recording exists, the agent's account of a careful, well-run conversation carries far less weight than the recording would have carried by itself. Verify current recording scope, retention duration and announcement duties for the plan year and for each state involved.

included: which calls fall in the recording obligation class and the announcement duty
storage, naming, access control, retention duration and retrieval speed
the evidentiary role of a recording when an allegation arrives
excluded: specific retention durations and state consent particulars, which must be verified for the plan year and jurisdiction
what is said during the enrollment conversation itself, which belongs to the enrollment knowledge base

pros.claim: A complete recording converts a he-said-she-said allegation into a resolvable question of fact, usually in the agent's favor when the call was run well
pros.example: a complaint alleging a plan was described as covering a specific doctor being closed by the recording of the actual exchange

pros.claim: Recording changes behavior for the better, because agents phrase things more carefully when the file exists
pros.example: an agent naturally restating the disclosure sentence at the top of every call once recordings became routine

cons.claim: Recording infrastructure has real cost, failure modes and privacy obligations, and a partially working system is a trap
cons.example: a mobile call path that silently failed to record for two weeks while the office line worked perfectly

cons.claim: The announcement can chill an already-suspicious beneficiary if it is delivered as legal boilerplate rather than explained
cons.example: an opening line about recording that makes a first-time caller hesitate and hang up

failure_modes: recording only the office line while most calls happen on a mobile phone
letting an automatic storage purge run shorter than the required retention period
storing recordings without access control although they contain health and identity information
acceptance_tests: a test call on every channel in use produces a retrievable recording with the correct naming, and the recording can be located and produced within the carrier's stated response window
retention settings are documented and demonstrably longer than the longest applicable required period, with access limited and logged
revisit_triggers: recording scope, retention duration or announcement duties change for the plan year or in any state used
a channel, phone system or storage provider changes
a retrieval request cannot be met inside the deadline

base.update_signal: recording scope, retention or announcement duties change, a channel or storage provider changes, or a retrieval request misses its deadline

nodes.definition: Run events by first deciding, then honestly advertising, which class the event belongs to, because the class determines what may happen in the room. An educational event is advertised as educational, teaches how the program and the coverage classes work, and does not promote or compare specific plans, does not collect scope agreements or enrollment applications, and does not put plan-specific materials on the table. A marketing or sales event does discuss plan-specific content and may lead to enrollment, and in exchange carries advertising, reporting and conduct requirements including reporting to carriers on their schedule and reporting cancellations. The operating discipline is to advertise the class accurately, keep any sign-in voluntary and say so out loud, bring only materials matching the declared class, hold refreshments and giveaways inside the nominal-value class and never tie them to enrollment, and have a compliant path ready for the person who asks to enroll at an educational event, which is to capture their request to be contacted and meet separately.
