The recurring hazard is drift: a well-attended educational session where the audience keeps asking plan-specific questions becomes a sales event by content no matter what the flyer said, so the agent needs a prepared redirect. Verify current event definitions, reporting windows and advertising requirements each plan year.

included: the two event classes, what each permits and forbids, and how the class is declared in advertising
reporting and cancellation duties and the voluntary sign-in practice
the drift hazard and the prepared redirect to a separate appointment
excluded: the individual appointment that follows an event, which runs under the scope-of-appointment and enrollment rules
specific reporting windows and nominal-value thresholds, which are verified for the plan year

pros.claim: Declaring the class honestly makes the whole event defensible even when it is later reviewed or secretly shopped
pros.example: an educational session whose flyer, materials and sign-in practice all match when a carrier reviewer attends unannounced

pros.claim: Educational events reach exactly the people who most need a neutral explanation before anyone sells them anything
pros.example: a library session that fills with people who have been avoiding the mail pile and want to understand it once

cons.claim: Educational events convert slowly and cannot be closed in the room, so they demand patience and a compliant follow-up path
cons.example: a full room producing only a handful of contact requests to meet separately later

cons.claim: Drift is easy and often driven by the audience rather than the agent, and the class is judged by what actually happened
cons.example: attendees asking which plan the agent would pick until the session has become plan-specific in substance

failure_modes: advertising an educational event while planning to take applications afterward in the same room
using a sign-in sheet that looks mandatory or that doubles as a contact-permission form without saying so
missing the carrier reporting window or failing to report a cancellation
acceptance_tests: for each event the advertised class, the materials list, the sign-in practice and the reporting record are consistent and on file before the event date
the redirect for an attendee who asks to enroll at an educational event is written into the run sheet and produces a documented contact request rather than an application
revisit_triggers: event definitions, reporting windows or advertising requirements change for the plan year
an event drifts out of its declared class or a venue changes the setting rules
a carrier changes how events must be reported or approved

base.update_signal: event definitions, reporting windows or advertising rules change, or a hosted event drifts out of its declared class

nodes.definition: Build the steady local presence that makes a Medicare practice sustainable, inside the contact rules rather than around them. What works and is permitted: being the person who teaches the free session on how the program works at the library, senior center or church hall; relationships with pharmacists, senior-service agencies, tax preparers and financial professionals who send along people who have asked for a referral; an accurate, unglamorous community reputation built over years; and cooperation with the neutral state assistance program class rather than competing with it. What the rules constrain: presence inside health-care settings is limited to common areas and requires the provider's agreement, since activity where care is delivered is prohibited; providers themselves must not steer patients toward particular plans, so a partnership that has a clinic recommending the agent's plans is a problem for both parties; referral arrangements must not become payments that induce enrollment, and any permitted referral-compensation class is narrow, carrier-specific and rule-specific; and a referred person is not a consented contact until they themselves ask. The judgment to hold is that a partner's enthusiasm is never authority, and the agent, not the partner, owns whatever contact follows. Verify referral-compensation and provider-setting rules currently, since both are actively enforced.

included: permitted community venues, partner relationships and the common-area limit in health-care settings
the inducement line on referral arrangements and the non-steering duty of provider partners
the rule that a referred person must ask before being contacted
excluded: referral generation from an existing served book and retention-driven word of mouth, which belong to the renewal and retention knowledge base
specific referral-fee amounts or permitted structures, which must be verified with the carrier and current rules

pros.claim: A visible neutral presence generates inbound requests, which are the cleanest consent artifact that exists
pros.example: a pharmacist telling a customer to call the agent, and the customer making the call herself

pros.claim: Community teaching compounds year over year in a way purchased leads never do, and it costs the practice its time rather than its integrity
pros.example: the same senior center session drawing a larger room each year because previous attendees told friends

cons.claim: Partners do not know the rules and will cheerfully offer arrangements that would be prohibited inducements or prohibited steering
cons.example: a clinic manager proposing to hand out the agent's card with every discharge packet and asking what the agent will do for the clinic in return

cons.claim: Community presence is slow and hard to attribute, so it is chronically under-invested next to purchased leads that produce visible names this week
cons.example: cutting a standing monthly session in favor of a lead buy in a season where the pipeline felt thin

failure_modes: letting a partner hand over a list of names to call
setting a table beyond the common area of a retail pharmacy or clinic
agreeing to any per-enrollment thank-you with a referral partner
acceptance_tests: every partner relationship is documented with what the partner may and may not do, the non-steering and non-inducement terms, and the requirement that referred people initiate contact themselves
for each community venue used, the permitted location within the venue and the venue's agreement are on file before the activity happens
revisit_triggers: a partner proposes a compensation or exclusivity arrangement
provider-setting or referral-compensation rules change or an enforcement action addresses them
a referred contact complains that they never asked to be contacted

base.update_signal: a partner proposes a new arrangement, provider-setting or referral rules change, or a referred contact reports they never asked to be contacted

nodes.definition: Treat every beneficiary-facing digital surface as regulated material with a version, an approval and an expiry date. The practice website, landing pages, lead forms, social posts, paid advertising, video, email templates and even a business card can fall into the marketing class the moment they mention plan benefits, costs, comparisons or ratings, which triggers the required disclaimer, the prohibited-claim rules and the applicable review or submission path through the carrier or the program. The operating system that keeps this manageable is a content inventory with owner, class, approval identifier and plan-year stamp; lead-form language that plainly states what the person is requesting so that it creates a real consent record; a claims discipline that bans superlatives, scare hooks, countdown-style urgency and any implication of government affiliation; review lead time built into the content calendar rather than discovered at publication; and a plan-year turn ritual that pulls or updates every prior-year asset, because a page still describing last year's benefits is a live misrepresentation regardless of intent. Digital surfaces also age invisibly, so the inventory carries a review date per item. Review paths, submission requirements and disclaimer wording change by contract year and by carrier, so re-verify before each season rather than reusing last year's assumptions.

included: the content inventory with class, approval identifier, plan-year stamp and review date
lead-form consent language and the claims discipline for digital copy
the plan-year turn ritual that retires or re-approves prior-year assets
excluded: the substance of plan comparisons published for beneficiaries, which must follow the enrollment knowledge base and carrier-approved content
carrier-specific submission mechanics, which are read from that carrier's current instructions

pros.claim: A versioned inventory makes the annual turn mechanical instead of a scramble to remember what is live
pros.example: pulling every asset carrying last plan year's stamp on a single scheduled afternoon before the new season

pros.claim: Honest lead-form language produces consent artifacts that actually hold up, which raises the quality of the whole pipeline
pros.example: a form that states plainly that a licensed agent will call about Medicare plan options and records the timestamp and page

cons.claim: Review lead time is at odds with how digital content is normally made, and the temptation to post first is constant
cons.example: a topical post about a local plan change that would be stale by the time review clears

cons.claim: Digital assets accumulate across platforms and quietly escape the inventory, especially old posts and third-party directory listings
cons.example: an outdated profile on a listing site still advertising a plan class the practice no longer carries

failure_modes: editing an approved asset and leaving the old approval identifier attached
letting prior plan-year content stay live past the year turn
using stock marketing copy from a vendor without checking it against the prohibited-claims list
acceptance_tests: the content inventory lists every live beneficiary-facing asset across every platform with class, approval identifier, plan-year stamp and last review date
a spot check of three live assets shows current-year approval, the required disclaimer where applicable, and no prohibited claim
revisit_triggers: the plan year turns or a carrier changes disclaimer or submission requirements
a new platform, format or advertising channel is adopted
an asset is edited, or a listing or profile is discovered outside the inventory

base.update_signal: the plan year turns, a carrier changes disclaimer or review requirements, or an unlisted live asset is discovered

nodes.definition: Operate on the standing assumption that a meaningful share of the people this practice serves are older adults, people with disabilities, and people under health or financial stress, and build the protective habits into the appointment itself rather than into a policy nobody reads. The habits are concrete. Disclosure comes first: who the agent is, which carriers are represented, that the practice does not offer every plan available in the area, and how the agent is paid if asked. Pacing lets the person read and ask, with a written summary they keep and permission to take days. Comprehension is checked by invitation rather than quiz, asking the person to say back in their own words what the plan would mean for their doctor and their prescriptions. Framing excludes fear: no manufactured deadlines beyond the real enrollment-period ones, no implication that benefits will be lost without action, no same-day pressure when the person is uncertain. Family involvement is welcomed while the decision stays with the beneficiary, and any authorized-representative status is documented properly rather than assumed from presence in the room. Finally there is a stop rule: when signals of confusion, coercion or diminished capacity appear, the meeting ends without an application and routes to a second conversation, a documented representative, or the neutral state assistance program. This is the one area where a technically compliant practice can still do real harm.

included: disclosure-first opening, pacing, comprehension checks and the no-fear framing rule
family and authorized-representative handling and the documentation it requires
the stop rule and its referral destinations
excluded: clinical or capacity determinations, which are not the agent's to make and belong to clinicians and legal processes
the plan comparison content itself, which belongs to the enrollment knowledge base

pros.claim: Unpressured pacing produces enrollments that survive, because a person who understood the plan does not disenroll in surprise a month later
pros.example: a beneficiary who took the written summary home for a week and then enrolled without confusion about her specialist

pros.claim: A written stop rule gives the agent permission to walk away from a case that would otherwise be closed under family pressure
pros.example: ending a meeting where an adult child kept answering for a mother who looked lost, and offering a follow-up with proper documentation

cons.claim: Slower, protective practice loses cases to agents who close on the first visit, and the cost lands entirely on the careful agent
cons.example: a beneficiary who took a week to decide being enrolled in the meantime by a call-center agent who never paused

cons.claim: Capacity signals are ambiguous and the agent is not qualified to judge them, so the stop rule will sometimes fire on someone perfectly capable and feel patronizing
cons.example: pausing with a person whose hearing difficulty was mistaken for confusion

failure_modes: letting a family member effectively make the decision because it is faster and everyone in the room seems comfortable
using urgency language that implies coverage will be lost without acting today
proceeding after comprehension checks plainly failed because the paperwork was already open
acceptance_tests: the opening disclosure, the comprehension-check invitation and the stop rule appear verbatim in the appointment script and in the recorded calls sampled for review
any case where the stop rule fired shows what happened next: a second conversation, a documented representative, or a referral, with no application submitted in between
revisit_triggers: a complaint or audit finding involves pressure, comprehension or a third party acting for a beneficiary
rules on authorized representatives, disclosures or senior-consumer protection change
the practice enters a segment with different comprehension or language needs

base.update_signal: a complaint or finding involves pressure or comprehension, representative and senior-protection rules change, or the practice enters a segment with different language or comprehension needs

nodes.definition: Define what file must exist for every beneficiary interaction and build the habit that creates it while the interaction is still happening. The per-interaction record holds the consent artifact and its source, the scope agreement with its date and signature method, the recording identifier for covered calls, the versioned materials actually shown with their approval identifiers, dated notes stating what was discussed and what the beneficiary said they wanted and why, any disclosures made, and the outcome including the cases where nothing was submitted, since a documented no-sale is evidence of a well-run process. Around the record sit the custody rules: identity, health and Medicare-number data are handled under privacy obligation classes with access control, encryption at rest, clean-desk and clean-car practice, secure transmission, and a destruction schedule that runs after the retention period rather than before it. The design principle is contemporaneity - notes written the same day are evidence, while notes reconstructed months later during an inquiry are merely argument, and everyone reviewing them knows the difference. Retention durations, permitted signature methods and privacy obligations differ by carrier, state and rule year, so the file standard is set from current requirements and re-checked each season rather than inherited.

included: the required artifact list per interaction and the contemporaneity habit
custody, access control, transmission and destruction rules for identity and health data
retention duration classes per artifact and the annual re-check of the standard
excluded: the substance of the recommendation recorded in the notes, which belongs to the enrollment knowledge base
post-enrollment service records over the life of the account, which belong to the renewal and retention knowledge base

pros.claim: A complete contemporaneous file usually ends an inquiry quickly, because the record answers the question before anyone has to remember anything
pros.example: a complaint closed on the strength of the dated consent artifact, the scope agreement and the note written that evening

pros.claim: Standardizing the artifact list removes judgment from a moment when the agent is tired and the day is over
pros.example: a checklist that fills automatically in the same order after every appointment, including the no-sale cases

cons.claim: Documentation competes directly with selling time in the densest weeks of the year, which is exactly when it is most likely to be skipped
cons.example: four appointments in a day producing four sets of notes that all get postponed to a weekend that never comes

cons.claim: Holding health and identity data creates its own custodial risk and obligations that a paper-and-phone practice underestimates
cons.example: a folder of applications left in a car overnight between appointments

failure_modes: reconstructing notes weeks later when an allegation arrives
storing artifacts across a phone, a laptop and a paper folder with no single index
destroying records on a generic schedule that is shorter than the required retention period
acceptance_tests: a randomly chosen interaction from the last month produces every required artifact from one index, with dates showing the notes were written the same day
the custody rules are demonstrable: access is limited and logged, transmission is secure, and the destruction schedule is documented as longer than the longest applicable retention requirement
revisit_triggers: retention, signature-method or privacy requirements change for a carrier, state or plan year
an audit or complaint response reveals an artifact class the file did not contain
the practice changes tools for notes, storage or signatures

base.update_signal: retention, signature or privacy requirements change, an audit reveals a missing artifact class, or the practice changes its notes, storage or signature tooling

nodes.definition: Know the oversight machinery that watches this business and how to behave when it engages, before it engages. The mechanisms include carrier call monitoring and agent scorecards, secret-shopper contacts at events and by phone, the complaint pathway by which a beneficiary complaint reaches the plan and then the program as a tracked record with a response deadline, state insurance-department inquiries, and periodic carrier audits of files, materials and events. The response discipline is specific: acknowledge inside the carrier's deadline; pull the file, the recording and the consent artifact before writing a single sentence; answer the precise allegation factually without editorializing about the complainant or their family; state what the record shows and, where relevant, what it does not; and where a real error occurred, say so plainly, describe the correction made for the beneficiary, and describe the process change that prevents recurrence. The escalation ladder is real and runs from retraining and probation through commission holds and termination for cause with a carrier to state disciplinary action, and one termination for cause tends to close doors at other carriers. The operating stance is to treat every finding, including a dismissed one, as a signal to fix the process that produced the exposure rather than as an accusation to be argued down.

included: the oversight mechanisms and what each one examines
the response sequence, tone and deadline discipline for an allegation
the escalation ladder and the process-fix stance toward every finding
excluded: legal representation and any decision to contest a regulatory action, which belongs to counsel
errors-and-omissions claim handling mechanics, which belong to the carrier of that coverage

pros.claim: A rehearsed response sequence prevents the two responses that make everything worse: silence past the deadline and an emotional letter about the complainant
pros.example: a same-week factual reply built from the recording and the consent artifact instead of a defensive narrative

pros.claim: Treating findings as process signals turns oversight into the practice's cheapest source of improvement
pros.example: a dismissed complaint about a confusing explanation leading to a rewritten section of the appointment script

cons.claim: Complaints arrive for reasons outside the agent's control, including confusion, family disagreement and plan-level service failures, so volume is a noisy signal
cons.example: a complaint generated when a beneficiary's pharmacy costs changed at the plan year and the family blamed the agent

cons.claim: Responding well consumes time in the busiest weeks and cannot be delegated, since the response is the agent's own account
cons.example: a deadline landing during the peak of the enrollment window with three appointments already booked that day

failure_modes: missing the carrier response deadline and converting a routine inquiry into a compliance action
answering from memory before pulling the file and the recording
arguing about the complainant's character rather than addressing the allegation
acceptance_tests: a written response playbook exists with the deadline, the evidence-pull order, the tone rules and the escalation ladder, and any past response can be shown to have followed it
each closed finding, including dismissed ones, has a recorded process change or an explicit recorded decision that none was warranted
revisit_triggers: any complaint, secret-shop result, monitoring score or audit request arrives
a carrier changes its response deadlines or audit scope
a pattern emerges across findings pointing at one script, asset, setting or lead source

base.update_signal: a complaint, secret shop, monitoring score or audit arrives, a carrier changes deadlines or audit scope, or findings form a pattern around one script, asset or lead source

nodes.definition: Compose everything above into one pre-season gate that must be green before any plan-year contact happens. The gate is a list with evidence rather than a feeling, and it checks: annual certification complete and transmitted; per-carrier product certification and ready-to-sell confirmed for each product, state and plan year; licenses and appointments current with dates; errors-and-omissions coverage in force; the current-year compensation schedules retrieved and filed; the rule map refreshed against the current contract-year text; scripts, disclaimers and the required disclosure language updated; every marketing asset either re-approved for the new plan year or pulled; the recording system tested end to end on every channel; consent, scope and interaction-file templates in place; the event calendar built and reported to carriers on their schedule; and prior-year materials retired. What makes it a gate rather than a checklist is the stopping rule: a red item stops the corresponding activity rather than the whole practice, so an agent who is ready to sell with two carriers markets those two and stays silent about the third until it clears. The gate is rebuilt each plan year from current requirements, because last year's green is a record of the past and not evidence about the season about to start.

included: the pre-season checklist with evidence per item
the partial-stop rule that halts only the activity a red item touches
the annual rebuild of the gate from current requirements
excluded: the enrollment-period calendar and the demand planning built on it, which belong to the enrollment knowledge base
mid-year service and renewal activity, which belongs to the renewal and retention knowledge base

pros.claim: One dated gate converts a dozen scattered readiness questions into a single decision the practice can defend later
pros.example: a signed gate record showing which two carriers were sellable on the day the marketing window opened and which one was not

pros.claim: The partial-stop rule keeps the practice working during the season instead of freezing everything over one unresolved item
pros.example: marketing the two cleared carriers while a third carrier's product module is finished the following week

cons.claim: A gate applied under season pressure invites quiet exceptions, and one waived item is how the whole discipline erodes
cons.example: letting a not-yet-approved flyer go out because the event is Saturday and approval is expected Monday

cons.claim: Composing the gate late in the pre-season leaves no time to fix what it finds, which turns the gate into a delay rather than a control
cons.example: discovering an expired appointment two days before the window opens when the filing takes longer than that

failure_modes: running the gate as a memory exercise instead of an evidence check
waiving items under season pressure without recording the waiver or its expiry
carrying last plan year's completed gate forward as if it still described the practice
acceptance_tests: the gate record for the current plan year exists with evidence and a date beside every item, and every red item names the specific activity it stops
the gate is dated far enough ahead of the marketing window that a failed item could still be remediated before contact begins
revisit_triggers: the plan year turns or a new contract-year rule set is published
any authority, material approval or system check goes red mid-season
a carrier is added, suspended or removed during the plan year

base.update_signal: the plan year turns, a new contract-year rule set is published, or an authority, approval or system check goes red mid-season

edges.why_related: which state authorities license the person, and what they require, is read off the rule map before any license work starts
the annual certification requirement and its deadlines belong to the program and carrier layers the map identifies
the classification test is an application of the program layer the map identifies, and the review path it routes to comes from the carrier layer
the stop rule and the referral destinations are the charter's refusal language applied to the moments where a beneficiary may be vulnerable
the shelf must be able to cover what the charter says the practice offers, and the charter supplies the referral sentence for needs it cannot cover
an upline is evaluated for the states and lines the practice is actually licensed in, so the license footprint frames the choice
carriers contract and appoint only producers who hold a current license in the line and state, so licensing precedes contracting
which carriers the practice can actually reach is bounded by the hierarchy it writes under and by release constraints on moving
the shelf decision determines which carriers are contracted, so deciding it first prevents contracting the wrong set and certifying for it
a carrier only opens its product training and ready-to-sell path to a contracted and appointed producer
carriers gate their own product modules behind the completed annual industry certification for the plan year
the compensation schedule that must be read and reconciled is an artifact of the specific carrier contract that was signed
ready-to-sell status is the field the register exists to record and re-verify before any appointment
license status and expiry are register fields, and their per-state dates are the ones most likely to lapse unnoticed
whether an outreach is marketing decides which contact permissions and disclaimers must exist before it happens
most prohibitions attach specifically to marketing-class acts and materials, so the inventory is organized around the classification
the recording obligation attaches to calls in the marketing, sales and enrollment chain, so the classification decides which calls are covered
every digital surface is classified first, and only marketing-class items enter the review and approval path
the appointment can only be scheduled with someone whose permission to be contacted already exists, and the scope agreement narrows that permission to product types
vendor vetting exists to prove that the consent standard the practice holds itself to was actually met upstream
the event class rules are the prohibitions applied to a room: what may be said, collected, offered and advertised
the community program is largely built from events, so the class rules govern what the practice can offer a venue or partner
the scope agreement is one of the artifacts the interaction file must hold, with its date, method and retention period
every response to a complaint, audit or inquiry is assembled from the interaction file, so the response is only as good as the file
the gate reads its authority items straight from the register rather than re-deriving them under season pressure
the scope agreement must be explained and paced as a consumer protection rather than pushed across the table, which constrains how and when it is taken
the practice may only present or advertise plans it is currently ready to sell, which bounds what any event or partner conversation can cover
a vendor's advertising and scripts must satisfy the same prohibition list the agent is held to, because the resulting contact is attributed to the agent
knowing which carriers and products pay what creates a pull toward a narrower, better-paying shelf exactly where breadth protects the beneficiary
edges.resolution_rule: the shelf is sized and the comparison ordered by beneficiary need only; compensation is never a comparison factor and never a tiebreak, and any shelf change justified by pay is rejected and recorded as rejected

edges.why_related: every carrier added to protect against steering adds annual certification, product training and portal load that competes for the same pre-season weeks
edges.resolution_rule: breadth required to serve documented local need wins over certification convenience; if the calendar cannot absorb it, cut the least need-relevant carrier rather than skipping or deferring certification, and record which need became a referral instead

edges.why_related: lead volume and speed pull against the requirement that every contact rest on a verifiable, in-scope, unexpired consent artifact
edges.resolution_rule: consent evidence wins without exception: any record whose consent language, timestamp and origin cannot be produced is not contacted regardless of what it cost, and the vendor is suspended pending evidence

edges.why_related: venues and partners want a session that produces enrollments in the room, which is precisely what the educational class forbids
edges.resolution_rule: the declared event class governs the room; if the partner wants enrollment activity, the event is advertised and reported as a marketing or sales event or the practice declines, and no educational session is converted after it is advertised

edges.why_related: the conduct classes on the inventory are the ones that actually generate complaints, secret-shop failures and carrier actions when they are crossed
pressure, confusion and family disputes around an older beneficiary are the dominant source of complaints, so the safeguard practice directly moves complaint volume
the scope agreement is settled before the covered conversation begins, and the recording then captures the conversation that stays inside it
each finding, dismissed or upheld, tells the practice which prohibition its scripts and habits sit closest to, and the inventory and rehearsal list are updated from that
complaint and opt-out clustering by lead source is the earliest reliable evidence that a vendor's consent trail is fictional, and it retires the vendor
what the gate found red, and how late it was found, sets when certification and product training are scheduled in the following plan year
both are recurring authority-maintenance obligations with their own issuers, expiry calendars and proving artifacts, and both fail the same way when treated as one-time events

conflict_axes.name: compliance_dominance_versus_growth_pressure
conflict_axes.description: Every acquisition idea that would grow the practice faster - more contacts, quicker meetings, looser materials - runs against a rule set whose breach can end carrier access entirely.
poles: maximize reach and speed during the short selling season
hold every rule line even when it costs the season
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compliance dominates growth in every conflict; growth is planned inside the rule set by starting earlier and building community demand, never by shaving a rule

conflict_axes.name: lead_volume_versus_consent_provenance
conflict_axes.description: The cheapest and largest lead supplies are exactly the ones whose consent trail cannot be produced, while verifiable sources are scarcer, slower and more expensive.
poles: buy volume and work it fast
contact only records with producible consent
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: no producible consent artifact means no contact; spend the saved money on community presence and inbound requests, which are the cleanest consent that exists

conflict_axes.name: shelf_breadth_versus_certification_capacity
conflict_axes.description: A shelf wide enough to serve local need honestly costs annual certification, product training and portal maintenance that all land in the same pre-season weeks.
poles: carry every carrier the area needs
carry only what can be certified deeply and on time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: size the shelf from documented local need, start certification early enough to absorb it, and where the calendar still cannot, drop the least need-relevant carrier and write down the referral path that replaces it

conflict_axes.name: compensation_salience_versus_need_driven_comparison
conflict_axes.description: The agent must understand compensation well enough to verify and explain it, and that understanding is precisely what threatens a need-driven comparison.
poles: know the schedules in detail
keep pay entirely out of the recommendation
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: learn compensation as a mechanism and quarantine it with a written no-steering rule plus a periodic review of how enrollments distribute across the shelf

conflict_axes.name: education_value_versus_event_class_line
conflict_axes.description: The most useful thing an agent can do for a room of beneficiaries is answer their real questions, and their real questions are usually plan-specific, which converts an educational event into a sales event by content.
poles: answer whatever the room asks
hold the declared educational class
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer at the class level and redirect plan-specific questions to a separately arranged appointment with a captured contact request, or advertise and report the event as a marketing event from the start

conflict_axes.name: appointment_speed_versus_documentation_completeness
conflict_axes.description: Consent artifacts, scope agreements, recordings and same-day notes take time out of the densest weeks of the year, when the pull toward doing them later is strongest.
poles: see more beneficiaries per day
complete the file while the interaction is live
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: build documentation into the appointment itself rather than after it, and treat a missing artifact as a stop rather than a backlog item, since a reconstructed note is argument and a contemporaneous one is evidence

conflict_axes.name: warm_persuasion_versus_vulnerable_consumer_protection
conflict_axes.description: The skills that make an agent trusted and effective - warmth, confidence, momentum - are the same ones that can carry an uncertain older beneficiary past their own comprehension.
poles: close while the trust is warm
slow down until comprehension is demonstrated
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: comprehension and unpressured pacing dominate closing momentum; when signals of confusion or coercion appear the stop rule fires and no application is taken that day

conflict_axes.name: hierarchy_support_versus_book_portability
conflict_axes.description: The organizations that supply the most support tend to ask for compensation assignment, production commitments and release terms that reduce the practice's freedom to reshape its shelf later.
poles: take the support and the leads
preserve release and assignment freedom
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read release, dormancy and assignment clauses before signing and price the support against the cost of being unable to add a needed carrier for a full waiting period

conflict_axes.name: publishing_speed_versus_material_review_lag
conflict_axes.description: Timely digital content wins attention, while marketing-class material must sit in a review queue that does not care about the news cycle or the length of the season.
poles: publish while it is relevant
publish only what is approved and current-year stamped
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep a stock of pre-approved evergreen education for speed, put review lead time in the content calendar, and never publish the draft written while waiting

conflict_axes.name: family_involvement_versus_beneficiary_autonomy
conflict_axes.description: The adult child who arranged the meeting is often the most engaged person in the room, and letting them run it is faster, easier and a quiet displacement of the person whose coverage it is.
poles: work with the engaged family member
keep the decision with the beneficiary
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: welcome the family member, address the beneficiary directly, verify comprehension with the beneficiary, and require documented authority before anyone acts on their behalf

edge_cases.description: A purchased lead arrives with a name and phone number but the vendor cannot produce the consent language, timestamp or originating page the consumer actually saw
edge_cases.trigger: a shared or aggregated lead is delivered without a verifiable consent trail
edge_cases.mitigation: do not contact the record, request the artifact in writing, suspend purchases from that source until it is produced, and treat the unusable spend as the cost of the vendor's failure rather than a reason to call

edge_cases.description: At an event advertised as educational, an attendee asks the agent to enroll her right there because she drove an hour and does not want to come back
edge_cases.trigger: an enrollment request inside an educational-class event
edge_cases.mitigation: explain plainly why the class of the event prevents it, capture a written contact request from her, and schedule a separate appointment with a scope agreement, offering the earliest slot including a same-week option

edge_cases.description: A meeting agreed as a supplement discussion turns when the beneficiary asks about drug coverage and an advantage-class plan a neighbor mentioned
edge_cases.trigger: a product class outside the signed scope is raised mid-appointment
edge_cases.mitigation: pause, document an expanded scope agreement before discussing the new class, and if the applicable timing rule prevents same-meeting expansion, schedule the second conversation rather than continuing

edge_cases.description: An adult son books the appointment, answers every question, and instructs the agent to enroll his mother, who says little and looks to him before each answer
edge_cases.trigger: a third party attempts to act for a beneficiary without documented authority
edge_cases.mitigation: address the beneficiary directly, ask her to describe in her own words what she wants, and require documented representative authority before anyone else acts for her; if comprehension is unclear, stop and reschedule with the documentation in place

edge_cases.description: Mid-conversation the beneficiary repeats the same question three times and cannot recall which plan she is currently in
edge_cases.trigger: comprehension or capacity signals fail during an appointment
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the stop rule: take no application, leave a written summary, offer a second conversation with a trusted person present, and name the neutral state assistance program as an alternative, recording what was observed and what was offered

edge_cases.description: A carrier flips ready-to-sell status off mid-season for a late license renewal while three appointments involving that carrier's plans are already booked
edge_cases.trigger: an authority field goes red after appointments are scheduled
edge_cases.mitigation: stop all activity involving that carrier immediately, tell the affected beneficiaries plainly that the practice cannot present that plan right now and what their alternatives are, remediate the status, and re-verify before rebooking

edge_cases.description: A clinic manager invites the agent to set up a table in the treatment waiting area and to leave brochures in exam rooms
edge_cases.trigger: marketing is invited into a setting where care is delivered
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the treatment-area and exam-room placement, offer common-area presence with the provider's written agreement if permitted, explain the non-steering constraint to the manager, and record what was agreed

edge_cases.description: A senior center advertises the agent's upcoming educational session in its newsletter as a free lunch where you can sign up for a better plan
edge_cases.trigger: a partner produces marketing about the practice that the practice never reviewed
edge_cases.mitigation: correct or withdraw the announcement before the date, restate the event class in writing to the partner, keep refreshments inside the nominal-value class and never tied to enrollment, and add a pre-approval clause to the partner agreement

edge_cases.description: A social post and a landing page describing last plan year's benefits are still live weeks into the new plan year
edge_cases.trigger: the plan-year turn passes without the asset inventory being swept
edge_cases.mitigation: pull the assets immediately, log the exposure window, re-approve or replace them for the current year, and move the sweep to a dated calendar item ahead of the turn with a named owner

edge_cases.description: A call that began as a routine service question turned into a plan discussion, and the recording system was not running on that channel
edge_cases.trigger: a covered conversation happens on an unrecorded channel
edge_cases.mitigation: document the gap contemporaneously with what was discussed, arrange to repeat the material portion on a recorded channel before anything is submitted, fix the channel coverage, and test every channel again

edge_cases.description: A complaint alleges the agent called without permission, while the practice holds a consent record the beneficiary does not remember creating
edge_cases.trigger: a complaint contradicts the practice's own consent artifact
edge_cases.mitigation: answer inside the deadline with the artifact, its timestamp and its origin, without disputing the person's memory, honor the opt-out immediately, and audit the source that produced the record for the same pattern in other leads

edge_cases.description: During a Medicare marketing appointment a long-standing client mentions worrying about final expenses and asks the agent to quote a life product on the spot
edge_cases.trigger: a non-health product is raised inside a marketing appointment
edge_cases.mitigation: decline to cross-sell in that appointment using the prepared line, note the interest, and arrange a separate meeting under its own agreement and only within the lines of authority the license actually carries

workflow.action: Write the practice scope and refusal charter
workflow.description: State what the practice offers, what it refuses, where out-of-scope questions go, and the sentence that keeps the enrollment decision with the beneficiary
workflow.artifact: practice charter with refusal categories and referral destinations
workflow.gate: the offered product classes, at least three refusal categories with their destinations, and the decision-ownership sentence are written and match every planned script and asset

workflow.action: Build the layered rule map for the contract year
workflow.description: Map program, state, channel and carrier layers against each ordinary act, with the published source and the date it was read
workflow.artifact: one-page rule map with per-act layer table and source citations
workflow.gate: at least six ordinary acts each carry their applicable layers, compliance evidence and a dated source, and the strictest-applicable precedence rule is stated

workflow.action: Establish and calendar the producer license footprint
workflow.description: Obtain or renew resident and nonresident licenses for every state where a beneficiary may be met and set the renewal and continuing-education reminders
workflow.artifact: per-state license register with dates and reminders
workflow.gate: every state in the plan has a row with line of authority, effective and expiry dates, continuing-education status and a verification date

workflow.action: Choose the upline and read the release terms before contracting
workflow.description: Compare organizations on release policy, compensation assignment, production terms and actual support, then sign deliberately and keep the executed copy
workflow.artifact: hierarchy decision memo with clause summary and the signed agreement
workflow.gate: release, dormancy, assignment and non-solicitation clauses are summarized with page references and at least one compared alternative is named

workflow.action: Size the carrier shelf against documented local need and write the no-steering guard
workflow.description: Inventory local provider systems, plan classes and common beneficiary situations, decide which carriers are needed, and record the referral rule for gaps
workflow.artifact: shelf justification with local-need inventory, gap list and the written no-steering rule
workflow.gate: each carrier on the shelf traces to a documented local need, gaps have a referral path, and the no-steering rule is written as a standing rule

workflow.action: Contract and appoint with each carrier on the shelf
workflow.description: Submit contracting with license evidence and screening, secure appointments per state under the applicable timing rule, and confirm errors-and-omissions coverage
workflow.artifact: contracting pack with writing numbers, appointment evidence and coverage dates
workflow.gate: every shelf carrier shows a signed contract, a writing number, per-state appointment evidence and current coverage, months ahead of the marketing window

workflow.action: Complete the annual certification and compliance modules
workflow.description: Book and pass the annual industry certification and the fraud, waste, abuse and compliance modules early enough to absorb a failed attempt
workflow.artifact: certification completion evidence with transmission confirmations per carrier
workflow.gate: completion is evidenced and confirmed in each carrier portal with enough calendar left for all downstream product training

workflow.action: Complete per-carrier product training and confirm ready-to-sell
workflow.description: Work each carrier's product modules and assessments, then verify the ready-to-sell flag per product, state and plan year in the carrier portal
workflow.artifact: ready-to-sell confirmations with portal verification dates
workflow.gate: every product the practice intends to present shows ready-to-sell for the current plan year and the relevant state, with the verification date recorded

workflow.action: Read the current-year compensation schedules and quarantine them
workflow.description: Retrieve each carrier's current schedule, classify the common case types, and write the plain answer to how the agent is paid
workflow.artifact: filed current-year schedules with a case-classification note and the how-I-am-paid answer
workflow.gate: schedules are on file with retrieval dates, a sample case classifies correctly, and the written answer uses mechanism language with no invented figures

workflow.action: Stand up the consent, scope, recording and interaction-file stack
workflow.description: Install consent capture with artifact storage, the scope agreement flow, tested recording on every channel, and the per-interaction file index with custody and retention rules
workflow.artifact: documentation and evidence system with templates, index, custody rules and retention settings
workflow.gate: a test interaction produces every required artifact from one index, a test call on each channel is retrievable, and retention exceeds the longest applicable requirement

workflow.action: Classify, review and stamp every beneficiary-facing asset and build the event calendar
workflow.description: Inventory every live asset, classify it, route marketing-class items to review with lead time, stamp the plan year, retire prior-year content, and declare and report each planned event class
workflow.artifact: content inventory with approvals and plan-year stamps plus the reported event calendar
workflow.gate: every live asset carries a class, a current-year approval where required and a review date, and each planned event has its declared class, materials list and carrier reporting on file

workflow.action: Run the annual readiness gate before any plan-year contact
workflow.description: Check every readiness item against evidence, record the date, and apply the partial-stop rule to anything red
workflow.artifact: dated readiness gate record with evidence per item and stopped-activity list
workflow.gate: every item is green with evidence or explicitly red with the specific activity it stops, and the record is dated far enough ahead of the window to remediate

dominance_rules.rule: Compliance dominates growth in every conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: a sustained violation pattern ends carrier access and the license itself, which forecloses all future growth, while a slower season is recoverable
dominance_rules.trigger: any acquisition, scheduling or content decision that would be faster or larger if a rule were shaved
dominance_rules.action: take the compliant path, record the opportunity that was declined and why, and look for the compliant substitute rather than an exception

dominance_rules.rule: No contact happens before provable authority exists
dominance_rules.rationale: license, appointment, certification and ready-to-sell are four separately expiring authorities and any gap makes the activity unauthorized regardless of intent
dominance_rules.trigger: an appointment is about to be booked or a plan is about to be discussed
dominance_rules.action: check the selling-authority register for that carrier, state, product and plan year and proceed only on a dated green

dominance_rules.rationale: unsolicited contact is both prohibited and the most common complaint allegation, and the burden of proof sits with the agent who made the contact
dominance_rules.trigger: a record cannot produce its consent language, timestamp and origin, or its permission has gone stale or names another topic or channel
dominance_rules.action: do not contact, hold the record out of the campaign, and demand the artifact from the source before any further use

dominance_rules.rule: The beneficiary's decision dominates the agent's opinion
dominance_rules.rationale: the practice is educational and the enrollment decision belongs to the beneficiary, who lives with the consequences of it
dominance_rules.trigger: a beneficiary asks what the agent would do, or a family member asks the agent to decide
dominance_rules.action: present the structured comparison, state the decision-ownership sentence from the charter, and refer questions outside scope to the named destination

dominance_rules.rule: Documented need dominates compensation in every comparison
dominance_rules.rationale: steering by pay is the central integrity failure of this business and it is usually invisible to the agent doing it
dominance_rules.trigger: two options are close, or a shelf or presentation-order decision would improve compensation
dominance_rules.action: decide on documented need, record the reason, and periodically review how enrollments distribute across the shelf for unexplained concentration

dominance_rules.rule: The strictest applicable rule governs when layers disagree
dominance_rules.rationale: program, state, channel and carrier layers apply simultaneously and permission in one is not permission in another
dominance_rules.trigger: a carrier policy, a state rule and the program rules give different answers for the same act
dominance_rules.action: follow the strictest applicable requirement and record which layer set the constraint and where its text was read

dominance_rules.rationale: audits, complaints and inquiries are decided on the record, and a contemporaneous artifact outweighs a confident recollection every time
dominance_rules.trigger: an interaction ends, or a response to an allegation is being prepared
dominance_rules.action: complete the file while the interaction is live, and answer any allegation only after pulling the artifact, the recording and the consent record

dominance_rules.rule: Vulnerable-consumer protection dominates the appointment agenda
dominance_rules.rationale: the population served is protected and frequently vulnerable, and a technically compliant sale to someone who did not understand it is still harm
dominance_rules.trigger: signals of confusion, coercion, fatigue or diminished capacity appear, or a third party begins deciding for the beneficiary
dominance_rules.action: fire the stop rule: take no application that day, leave a written summary, and route to a second conversation, a documented representative or the neutral assistance program

dominance_rules.rule: The declared event class dominates what happens in the room
dominance_rules.rationale: the class is what was advertised to attendees and reported to carriers, and conduct is judged against it rather than against intentions
dominance_rules.trigger: attendees or a venue partner push an educational session toward plan-specific promotion or enrollment
dominance_rules.action: answer at the class level, redirect to a separately arranged appointment, and never convert an event class after it has been advertised

dominance_rules.rule: A prohibited act stays prohibited even when the beneficiary asks for it
dominance_rules.rationale: consent from a beneficiary does not create authority the rules withhold, and the request is often the exact circumstance the prohibition anticipates
dominance_rules.trigger: a beneficiary or partner requests a prohibited act such as enrolling at an educational event, taking a neighbor's number, or discussing a non-health product in a marketing appointment
dominance_rules.action: use the prepared refusal line, offer the compliant alternative path, and record the request and the alternative offered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read the release, dormancy and compensation-assignment clauses before submitting the first carrier contract
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a sticky hierarchy assignment that blocks the practice from adding a locally necessary carrier for a full waiting period

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the shelf from documented local need before contracting, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: contracting and certifying a carrier set that does not match the area, then repeating the entire contracting and certification cycle

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete annual certification before the pre-season crunch rather than inside it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an exhausted attempt limit or a late transmission that pushes ready-to-sell past the opening of the marketing window

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture the consent artifact at the source, with its language, timestamp and origin, before any outreach
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an entire campaign of contacts that cannot be defended when a complaint arrives, and the wasted spend on unusable records

anti_rework_rules.rule: Classify a material as marketing or communication before producing it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: printing, publishing or mailing an asset that must then be recalled and re-made under review

anti_rework_rules.rule: Take the scope agreement ahead of the appointment by the required lead time, never at the table
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a meeting whose entire content becomes indefensible because the agreement was late or absent

anti_rework_rules.rule: Test recording on every channel actually used before the first sales call of the season
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering a silent recording gap only when a carrier requests a specific call that does not exist

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the selling-authority register before booking appointments
anti_rework_rules.prevents: appointments made for carriers, states or products the practice turns out not to be ready to sell, and the calls that cancel them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Vet a lead vendor's consent trail and advertising before the first purchase, not after the first complaint
anti_rework_rules.prevents: inheriting a vendor's prohibited advertising as the agent's own complaint record and having to unwind a whole source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Stamp every asset with its plan year and owner at creation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scramble at the plan-year turn to find which live pages, posts and profiles still describe last year's benefits

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new contract year's marketing and communication requirements are published
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the rule map, re-run the classification test over every asset and script, rebuild the prohibited-practices inventory from the current text, and re-approve or retire prior-year material

iteration_protocol.trigger: a certification lapses, a ready-to-sell flag flips off, or a carrier suspends the agent
iteration_protocol.action: freeze every activity touching that carrier, notify affected beneficiaries plainly, remediate the status, and re-verify the register before rebooking

iteration_protocol.trigger: a complaint, secret-shop finding or monitoring score arrives
iteration_protocol.action: respond from the file inside the deadline, root-cause the process that produced the exposure, and update the script, inventory or template that allowed it

iteration_protocol.trigger: complaints, opt-outs or unverifiable consent cluster around one lead source
iteration_protocol.action: suspend the source, re-verify the consent trail for every record already bought from it, remove the unverifiable records from all campaigns, and re-run the vendor vetting from the beginning

iteration_protocol.trigger: signals of confusion, pressure or third-party decision-making recur in a segment or setting
iteration_protocol.action: tighten the safeguard protocol for that segment, add the second-conversation default, and rehearse the stop rule and comprehension check before the next appointments

iteration_protocol.trigger: an audit or complaint response reveals an artifact class the interaction file did not contain
iteration_protocol.action: add the artifact to the required file standard, fix the template and the index, and apply it going forward while noting the gap period

iteration_protocol.trigger: the practice adds a state, a carrier or a product line
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the license, hierarchy, contracting, appointment and certification chain for the addition and refuse all marketing in it until the register shows a dated green

iteration_protocol.trigger: an event drifts out of its declared class, or a venue or partner produces unreviewed material about the practice
iteration_protocol.action: correct or withdraw the material, restate the class in writing to the partner, re-run the event playbook and add a pre-approval clause to the partner agreement

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because nothing else can be decided without knowing what the practice does and refuses and which rule layers govern each act; the authority stack follows in its forced order - license, hierarchy and shelf decision, contracting and appointment, annual certification, per-carrier product certification and ready-to-sell - because each step is a hard prerequisite of the next and the whole chain is summarized in the selling-authority register that answers the daily go or no-go question; the marketing-rule nodes then build on the classification test, since permission to contact, scope of appointment, prohibited practices, third-party marketing obligations and call recording all attach to acts classified as marketing; acquisition surfaces (events, community presence, digital material) sit above those rules because they are the places where the rules are actually tested by other people's expectations; the ethics and documentation nodes run alongside everything because vulnerable-consumer protection and a contemporaneous file are what make the rest survivable; and the readiness gate is last because it composes every prior item into one dated, evidenced go or no-go before the first beneficiary of the plan year is contacted.
